title: Building Writing Stamina
keyIdea: Different jobs need different kinds of writing. Instructions tell how to do something, in numbered steps that start with a bossy verb such as Fill or Mix. A recount tells what happened, in time order, with time words such as First, Next, After that and Finally, and verbs in the past tense, such as went and saw. A letter starts with Dear and a name and ends with Love from and your name. To keep writing for longer, plan first, then read back your last line and look at your plan when you get stuck.

kid: Pick the kind of writing for the job. How do you make a cake? Write instructions. What did you do at the zoo? Write a recount. Want to say thank you to Gran? Write a letter.
Instructions are steps, 1, 2, 3. Each step starts with a bossy verb, like Fill, Push or Mix. Do the steps in order, or it goes wrong.

A recount tells what you did. It is in the past: we went, we saw, we ate. Time words help: First, Next, After that, Finally. A letter starts with Dear Gran. The news goes in the middle. It ends with Love from and your name.
Long writing gets hard. Plan it first with pictures. If you get stuck, read back your last line. Then look at your plan to see what comes next.
adult: This matches Year 2 writing composition in the national curriculum for England. Pupils write about real events and their own experiences, and write for different purposes. They plan, say sentences aloud first, and re-read to check that the writing makes sense. In the US, CCSS W.1.3 asks first graders to recount two or more events in order, use temporal words to show the order and give a sense of closure. W.1.2 and W.2.2 cover informative and how-to writing.

Key terms: purpose (the job the writing does). Recount: a non-fiction retelling of real events in time order. Instructions: a procedural text with a goal, what you need and numbered steps. Imperative or command verbs are called bossy verbs in many classrooms. Temporal connectives, or time words, are first, next, after that and finally. Recounts use the past tense (went, saw, ate). A letter has a greeting (Dear …) and a sign-off (Love from …).

Common mistakes: slipping from the past tense into the future (we will see the lions) inside a recount. Putting Finally or First in the wrong place. Writing steps out of order, or as I-statements instead of commands. Putting the sign-off at the top of a letter. With stamina, the usual slip is rubbing out a whole page when stuck, which throws away good work. Stamina grows from a short plan of four pictures or key words, saying each sentence first, and a habit for getting unstuck: read back the last line, look at the plan, write the next bit. Praise the finished page more than neat letters.

In the lab your child matches writing jobs to forms. They order seed-planting steps and see the pot go wrong when a step comes too soon. They pick past-tense sentences with the right time words for a zoo recount, lay out a thank-you letter, and fill a page past two stuck moments. Every drag has a big button twin.

familyTip: After a day out, draw four quick pictures together of what happened, in order. Then your child writes one sentence for each, starting with First, Next, After that and Finally. If they get stuck, ask them to read back the last line and point to the next picture.

visual.caption: Recount or instructions? Drag each sentence, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: match writing jobs to instructions, recount or letter, put steps in order, write a recount, lay out a letter and keep going when stuck.

practice.prompt: You want to tell how to wash a bike. What do you write?
choices: A recount of a bike ride
practice.hint: The job is how to do something. Which kind of writing tells how to?
practice.explain: How to do something means instructions: numbered steps that start with bossy verbs, like Fill the bucket.

practice.prompt: Your recount plan has {n} pictures. You write one sentence for each picture. How many sentences will you write?
practice.hint: One sentence for each picture. Count the pictures.
practice.explain: One sentence for each of the {n} pictures makes {n} sentences. A plan tells you how much to write.

practice.prompt: Which sentence fits a recount of a trip to the farm?
practice.hint: A recount tells what already happened.
practice.explain: We fed the lambs is in the past, so it fits a recount. Feed the lambs is a bossy verb for instructions.

practice.prompt: You wrote {a} lines, then got stuck. You read back and kept going for {b} more lines. How many lines in all?
practice.hint: Add the lines before you got stuck to the lines after.
practice.explain: {a} lines and {b} more lines is {=a+b} lines. Reading back kept your first {a} lines safe.

pool.prompt: Which word is the best start for a recount?
pool.hint: Which time word comes at the start?
pool.explain: First starts a recount. Finally comes at the end. Dear starts a letter.

pool.prompt: Where does Love from Ben go in a letter?
pool.hint: It tells who wrote the letter.
pool.explain: Love from and your name go at the end. Dear and a name go at the top.

pool.prompt: Which is a bossy verb to start a step?
pool.hint: A bossy verb tells you what to do now.
pool.explain: Mix tells you what to do, so it can start a step. Mixed is in the past.

pool.prompt: You get stuck halfway down the page. What should you do?
choices: Read back my last line and look at my plan
pool.hint: Which one keeps the lines you already wrote?
pool.explain: Read back your last line and look at your plan. It shows what comes next, and you keep your work.

pool.prompt: You want to tell Grandad about your sports day and say hello. What do you write?
pool.hint: You are talking to one person.
pool.explain: Talking to one person is a letter: Dear Grandad, your news, then Love from and your name.

pool.prompt: Instructions have {n} steps. You have done 1 step. How many steps are left?
pool.hint: Take the 1 step you did away from {n}.
pool.explain: {n} take away 1 is {=n-1}, so {=n-1} steps are left. Do them in order.

pool.prompt: You write {n} lines today and {n} lines tomorrow. How many lines is that?
pool.hint: Add today's lines and tomorrow's lines.
pool.explain: {n} and {n} more is {=n+n} lines. A bit each day builds stamina.

pool.prompt: Which recount sentence is in the right tense?
choices: After that, we will eat lunch.
pool.hint: A recount tells what already happened.
pool.explain: We ate is in the past, so it fits a recount. We will eat has not happened yet.
